picks.company_brief: AeroVironment designs and makes drones, loitering munitions, and other uncrewed defense/robotic systems primarily for the U.S. military and allied governments.
picks.brief: Q1 FY2027 earnings (Sept 9) beat: revenue $480.5M vs $456.1M consensus, book-to-bill 1.4x, record backlog $1.5B (+37% YoY). JPMorgan raised its target to $210 (Overweight); Goldman cut to $285 (from $326) and Jefferies cut to $204 (from $229) despite the beat. ARK Investment bought 29,000 shares Sept 14. Stock is ~$159.95, down ~62% from its 52-week high of $417.86.
picks.why: A 37% YoY backlog surge and 1.4x book-to-bill on record counter-UAS/ISR contract wins signals accelerating forward revenue that the stock's steep drawdown hasn't caught up to, and JPMorgan's target hike alongside ARK's fresh buying suggests institutional recognition of that gap is just beginning.
picks.bull_case: Record backlog (+37% YoY) and a 1.4x book-to-bill ratio point to durable multi-year revenue growth from counter-drone and ISR demand; even the reduced Goldman/Jefferies targets imply 30%+ upside from $159.95.
picks.bear_case: Goldman and Jefferies both cut targets despite the beat, signaling margin or multiple-compression concerns baked into guidance; a name this reliant on U.S. defense budgets carries appropriations/timing risk.

picks.company_brief: Chewy is an online-first retailer of pet food, supplies, and pharmacy/vet services in the U.S. and Canada, generating recurring revenue through Autoship subscriptions.
picks.brief: Q2 FY2027 earnings (Sept 9): net sales +7.3% to $3.33B, adj. EPS $0.36, raised full-year outlook -- yet the stock fell sharply as Evercore ISI downgraded to In-Line, RBC and TD Cowen cut targets, and JPMorgan downgraded (Sept 11). Shares are ~$20.62, near their 52-week low and ~48% off the 52-week high of $40.55. Analyst consensus remains Buy with mean targets in the $28.82-$31.09 range.
picks.why: The stock fell despite a beat-and-raise quarter because sell-side downgrades are pricing in forward margin/spending-slowdown risk rather than the results just reported -- a classic sell-the-news reaction that has historically overshot before stabilizing once guidance proves out.
picks.bull_case: 7.3% net sales growth and a raised full-year outlook show the Autoship subscription base is still expanding; the ~40-50% gap to consensus target reflects sentiment, not the fundamentals just reported.
picks.bear_case: Multiple sell-side downgrades right after the print suggest analysts see margin or discretionary-pet-spending pressure building that guidance hasn't fully captured; sitting near 52-week lows can also mean the market is pricing in a real deceleration, not just overreacting.

picks.brief: New this cycle: Uber sold a ~$182.3M stake in Aurora Innovation (separate from its 2025 Aurora-linked bond deal) and launched a debut five-part EUR4.5B (~$5.2B) euro bond offering (priced Sept 7-9) to fund European expansion. Both ride alongside the already-logged $40M California wrongful-death ruling and CEO Khosrowshahi's $10M September share purchase. Price unchanged over the weekend at $70.50; technicals (web-sourced, medium confidence) show price below both the 50-day (~$75.19) and 200-day (~$75.11) SMA with RSI(14) ~47.8 (neutral). Analyst consensus remains Buy, target ~$101-105. Next earnings Nov 3, 2026.
picks.why: Trimming the Aurora stake for ~$182M while simultaneously launching a EUR4.5B multi-tranche euro bond shows Uber funding European growth with asset monetization and non-dilutive debt rather than equity, which typically signals management doesn't see the stock as attractively priced for raising capital via shares right now.
picks.bull_case: CEO insider buying, a Buy-rated analyst consensus near $103 (~46% above the current $70.50), and non-dilutive euro debt financing for European growth all support the long thesis; the Aurora stake sale further de-risks self-driving-related balance-sheet exposure.
picks.bear_case: Price remains below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a neutral-to-soft RSI, and the stock still carries an active $40M wrongful-death litigation overhang plus a widening debt load from the new euro bonds.

picks.company_brief: SoFi Technologies is a digital consumer fintech offering lending (student, personal, home), banking, investing, and increasingly blockchain-based payment and AI advisory products.
picks.brief: Piper Sandler initiated coverage Overweight/$22 and Scotiabank initiated Outperform/$25 (both Sept 2); Truist raised its target to $19 from $18, citing strong Q2 balance-sheet expansion (41% YoY revenue growth, 35% customer growth). Stock ~$16.96, ~49% off its 52-week high. A Citizens Bank lawsuit alleges SoFi poached employees and misused trade secrets.
picks.why: Two fresh sell-side initiations plus a target hike, all citing 41% revenue growth and stronger loan originations, suggest the price hasn't caught up to accelerating fundamentals -- though the pending Citizens Bank trade-secrets lawsuit is a real overhang on that thesis.
picks.bull_case: 41% YoY revenue growth and 35% customer growth back up three separate analyst target increases to $19-25, implying roughly 30% upside from $16.96.
picks.bear_case: A lawsuit alleging SoFi poached Citizens Bank staff and misused trade secrets could result in an adverse judgment or reputational damage to its lending/banking buildout; fintech names can re-rate hard on legal or regulatory headlines.
